would like to give my analysis of the below mentioned blog made by Dr. K. Vaishnavi ma'am with respect to my bimonthly blended assignemnt.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/karnativaishnavi.blogspot.com\/2021\/08\/cushings-syndrome.html?m=1\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/karnativaishnavi.blogspot.com\/2021\/08\/cushings-syndrome.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMy analysis is mainly with respect to the following aspects:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. What is the evidence of topical preparations of glucocorticoids causing Cushing's syndrome? Is it more as compared to oral or similar? Do other modes of administration have the same effects?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Evidence of the laboratory investigations used in the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Efficacy of the therapeutic interventions mentioned for this patient?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #741b47; font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EAddressing the 1st issue-\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. In this patient, order of priority of his problems according to me are as follows:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003EItchy, ring like lesions over trunk, arms, thigh and groin since 1 year\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EPurplish stretch marks over abdomen, limbs since 1 year\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EFacial puffiness and weight gain\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EFeeling low, not talking to anyone\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ELow back ache\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EPedal edema\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ELoss of libido, erectile dysfunction\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAll his findings are classic of CUSHING'S SYNDROME.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA) Itchy ring like lesions over trunk, arms, thigh and groin: Suggestive of TINEA CORPORIS ET CRURIS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfter going through the detailed analysis of the above mentioned blog, I think that this is the most important problem because this was the reason why he developed CUSHING'S SYNDROME in the first place.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe used CLOBETASOL OINTMENT over these lesions for approximately 1 year.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\"The risk increases based on factors that include glucocorticoid potency (see\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ca class=\"fig-table-link figpopup\" co-legend-rid=\"\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3775713\/table\/T1\/\" rid-figpopup=\"T1\" rid-ob=\"ob-T1\" style=\"background-color: white; color: #2f4a8b; cursor: pointer; display: inline-block; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; zoom: 1;\" target=\"table\"\u003ETable I\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E), the amount applied (affected body surface area is a surrogate measure), skin thickness and location (with eyelid and scrotum showing most penetration and the side of the foot the least), the presence of broken skin, the age of the patient (children have increased absorption), the use of occlusive dressings (which promote absorption), the type of vehicle (ointments increase penetration), and the duration of use. C\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003Eushing’s syndrome has been reported most often in infants receiving a class 1 agent (usually clobetasol)\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003EAlthough low doses of over-the-counter topical glucocorticoids are used\ncommonly and safely, it is known that systemic absorption of steroids from\ntopical preparations does occur and that at higher doses or with more\npotent preparations both adrenal axis suppression and Cushing’s syndrome\ncan occur.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #990000;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"\u0026quot;https:\/\/www.saem.org.ar\/departamentos\/departamento-neuroendocrinologia\/cushing-exogeno.pdf\u0026quot;\"\u003E\"https:\/\/www.saem.org.ar\/departamentos\/departamento-neuroendocrinologia\/cushing-exogeno.pdf\"\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\"It is now clear that significant\nsystemic effects of inhaled corticosteroids can be seen, although fewer than\nwith equivalent oral doses. These effects are dose-related and come in the\nform of adrenal suppression and Cushingoid stigmata, particularly bone,\nocular, and skin manifestations.\"\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB) Feeling low, not feeling like talking to anyone- suggestive of depression\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp id=\"__p4\" style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003EDepression, mood dysregulation, sleep disturbance and cognitive abnormalities are also observed in Cushing’s syndrome. The rates for each of these symptoms vary widely across studies. Depression is the most prevalent psychiatric disturbance in Cushing’s syndrome. A major depressive syndrome is seen in 50%–70% of the cases. Other associated features include anxiety in 12%–79% of the cases, as well as a rate of 3% for hypomania. Less common are features of psychosis and mania.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp id=\"__p7\" style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\"Glucocorticoid signalling\u0026nbsp;insufficiency\u0026nbsp;hypothesis suggests that hypercortisolaemia is an attempt to overcome primary glucocorticoid receptor resistance related to down-regulated glucocorticoid receptors. In contrast, the glucocorticoid signalling\u0026nbsp;overactivity\u0026nbsp;hypothesis for depression suggests there is overall increased net signalling via the glucocorticoid receptor. Changes in cortisol activity leading to decreased serotonin and increased dopamine cerebral activity have also been described.\"\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #990000;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3718650\/#:~:text=Depression%20is%20the%20most%20prevalent,mania%20%5B5%2C6%5D.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3718650\/#:~:text=Depression%20is%20the%20most%20prevalent,mania%20%5B5%2C6%5D.\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #741b47; font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EAddressing the 2nd issue:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe following study was done to check for the sensitivity of SLEEPING MIDNIGHT CORSTISOL in the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #990000;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/8548938\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/8548938\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-family: BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\"The aim of this study was to compare the sensitivity in the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome of a single in-patient sleeping midnight cortisol to a standard 48-hour in-patient low-dose dexamethasone suppression test (LDDST) during the same admission.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-family: BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIn this series of 150 cases, a single in-patient sleeping midnight cortisol above 50 nmol\/l had a 100% sensitivity for the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome, clearly different from normal subjects. In contrast, the low-dose dexamethasone suppression test had a sensitivity of 98% even when the drug was administered as an in-patient. We recommend that a low-dose dexamethasone suppression test should not be used alone for confirmation of Cushing's syndrome since it may miss 2% of cases.\"\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEfficacy of various investigations in the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEgfObAzhQH3yQYL0Ais0OuMt-bOQFlrYuTnfY-o25FJQ7XzX1zUK6a3uZa_n54Ie5J2t58BbmDUyHGUcofmUAG6ThH79_g4XnN5Ss2fzDKSGDZg-J4WlX2VSkDOF8bjmIx68rjGFfb7TwtwQBLiX7CvOxm8PkoFSYd3Np3E3_q3xU2omTdPjAsBLf4v=s654\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"388\" data-original-width=\"654\" height=\"190\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEgfObAzhQH3yQYL0Ais0OuMt-bOQFlrYuTnfY-o25FJQ7XzX1zUK6a3uZa_n54Ie5J2t58BbmDUyHGUcofmUAG6ThH79_g4XnN5Ss2fzDKSGDZg-J4WlX2VSkDOF8bjmIx68rjGFfb7TwtwQBLiX7CvOxm8PkoFSYd3Np3E3_q3xU2omTdPjAsBLf4v=s320\" width=\"320\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.scielo.br\/j\/abem\/a\/5hLj3WwC8CN6ctNdNn9Cyzg\/?lang=en#\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.scielo.br\/j\/abem\/a\/5hLj3WwC8CN6ctNdNn9Cyzg\/?lang=en#\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #741b47; font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EAddressing the 3rd issue-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient in our case received:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003ETAB. HISONE\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EINJ. HYDROCORTISONE (in cases of adrenal crisis)\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; border: 0px; color: #444444; font-family: \u0026quot;Lucida Grande\u0026quot;, Geneva, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-stretch: inherit; font-variant-east-asian: inherit; font-variant-numeric: inherit; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px 0px 1.42857em; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003ETreatment of exogenous cushing's syndrome is to decrease and eventually stop taking any corticosteroids which was also done in our patient. Suddenly stopping corticosteroids after taking them for a long time (usually more than 2 weeks) can result in a life-threatening condition called adrenal crisis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; border: 0px; color: #444444; font-family: \u0026quot;Lucida Grande\u0026quot;, Geneva, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-stretch: inherit; font-variant-east-asian: inherit; font-variant-numeric: inherit; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px 0px 1.42857em; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EInspite of tapering the dose of medication, his symptoms did not subside.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; border: 0px; color: #444444; font-size: 14px; font-stretch: inherit; font-variant-east-asian: inherit; font-variant-numeric: inherit; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px 0px 1.42857em; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003ETherefore, a probability of DOUBLE CUSHING'S SYNDROME was suspected. Though it is a very rare diagnosis, it should be considered in patients whose Cushing's syndrome related symptms do not subside even after stopping the steroid medication.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; border: 0px; color: #444444; font-size: 14px; font-stretch: inherit; font-variant-east-asian: inherit; She was initially aphasic but now she is able to speak.
